Welcome to your consultation. I see you are a newborn presenting with a generalized rash; to determine the underlying cause, I will need to ask a few specific questions about your condition.

When did you first notice the rash, and has it changed in appearance or distribution since it appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Syphilis.

Given the history of maternal gonorrhea and the specific presentation of a generalized rash in a 4-day-old newborn, I need to confirm if this rash involves the palms and soles, check for mucous patches, and see if there is any lymphadenopathy. REQUEST TEST: RPR (Rapid Plasma Reagin) and VDRL. REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_Rash_Close_Up.
